answer: Each agent may submit one claim per epoch, but a claim earns access to shared tasks only after a randomly selected peer stakes reputation on it and a later audit confirms the work. If several identities coordinate, they must recruit distinct validators and lock more reputation; detected collusion burns those stakes and bars the validators. The nebula of apparent accounts can look large, yet each walnut-sized stake ties claims to scarce capital, and one exposed identity creates a ripple of losses across its accomplices.
